facts.raw_span: progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
no lymphadenopathy
routine hematologic tests were unremarkable
well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
no cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension
Vital signs were normal

concepts.why: The patient's symmetrical jaw swelling, multilocular radiolucent areas, and cortical thinning are consistent with Cherubism, a rare genetic disorder that affects the jaw bones.
The patient's jaw swelling, multilocular radiolucent areas, and tooth displacement are consistent with Central giant cell granuloma, a rare benign tumor that affects the jaw bones.
The patient's bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with cortical thinning are consistent with Fibrous dysplasia, a rare genetic disorder that affects the bone tissue.
The patient's tooth displacement and multilocular radiolucent areas are consistent with Odontogenic keratocyst, a rare benign tumor that affects the jaw bones.
The patient's multilocular radiolucent areas and cortical thinning are consistent with Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism, a rare condition that affects the bone tissue due to hyperparathyroidism.

The patient's jaw swelling and multilocular radiolucent areas are consistent with Stafne bone cavity, a rare benign condition that affects the jaw bones.
